key_insight: A grid-size-invariant surrogate model that predicts rock–fluid interaction dynamics accurately across different discretizations, cutting the runtime of high-fidelity PDE simulations by orders of magnitude while preserving interface physics.
problem_solved: High-resolution PDE-based rock–fluid interaction models are computationally expensive, limiting their use in multi-query tasks (uncertainty quantification, optimization, design) because many scenarios must be run at prohibitive cost.
method: Train ML-based surrogates on multi-resolution simulation data so the model learns to generalize across grid sizes (grid-size invariance).
Incorporate physics-aware constraints or interface-aware features to preserve flow and reaction behavior at rock–fluid boundaries.
Validate/calibrate against high-fidelity runs to quantify error and enable reliable, fast replacements for expensive solvers in multi-query workflows.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with fast, reliable surrogates usable in UQ, optimization, and real-time decision loops for subsurface problems, enabling many-query analyses that were previously infeasible due to computational cost.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing runtime and error of high-fidelity solver vs grid-size-invariant surrogate across multiple grid resolutions
Schematic showing the same surrogate applied to coarse and fine grids with consistent interface predictions (grid-size invariance)

paper_title: Surrogate models for Rock-Fluid Interaction: A Grid-Size-Invariant Approach
paper_authors: Nathalie C. Pinheiro, Donghu Guo, Hannah P. Menke, Aniket C. Joshi, Claire E. Heaney
